hints: Focus on what controls gas density at the same temperature and pressure, think about mass per mole of mixture.
Notice the molar masses are $\text{H}_2 = 2$, $\text{He} = 4$ and $\text{CH}_4 = 16$, so methane is by far the heaviest.
Compare the average molar mass using % by molecules as mole fraction, the mixture with most heavy gas and least light $\text{H}_2$ will be densest.
walkthrough:
**Link density to average molar mass**

For gases under the same conditions, equal volumes contain equal moles. So density depends on mass per mole.

$$\text{density} \propto \text{average } M_r \text{ of mixture}$$

**Write the weighted average rule**

% by number of molecules is the same as % by moles. Multiply each % by its $M_r$ and add.

$$\text{average } M_r = \frac{(\% \text{H}_2 \times 2) + (\% \text{He} \times 4) + (\% \text{CH}_4 \times 16)}{100}$$

**Compare the planets without full calculator work**

$\text{CH}_4$ ($M_r = 16$) dominates the average even in small amounts. Uranus has the most $\text{CH}_4$ at 2.3% and relatively less very light $\text{H}_2$.

Quick check: Uranus $\approx (82.5 \times 2 + 15.2 \times 4 + 2.3 \times 16)/100 = 2.63$, which is higher than Jupiter $\approx 2.20$, Saturn $\approx 2.12$ and Neptune $\approx 2.52$.

**Conclude the densest mixture**

The largest average $M_r$ means the greatest mass per unit volume. That is the Uranus mixture.

options.A: Jupiter is almost all very light $\text{H}_2$ (89.8%) with some He and no $\text{CH}_4$. Its average $M_r$ is about 2.20, lighter than mixtures containing methane.
options.B: Neptune has more He and 1.0% $\text{CH}_4$, so its average $M_r$ of about 2.52 is high. But it has less $\text{CH}_4$ than Uranus, so it is second densest, not first.
options.C: Saturn has the most $\text{H}_2$ (96.3%) and the least He and $\text{CH}_4$. Its average $M_r$ of about 2.12 is the lowest, so it is the least dense. A common trap is to pick the highest % of one gas.
options.D: Uranus has the highest % of heavy $\text{CH}_4$ (2.3%, $M_r = 16$) combined with substantial He. Its average $M_r$ of about 2.63 is the greatest, so at the same T and p it has the greatest density.
